newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian Metals - Singapore copper premiums may slide.
newsitem.headline: Asian Metals - Singapore copper premiums may slide.

text.p: Singapore copper premiums could come under pressure up to mid-July with large shipments of metal headed for the city-state and with a Chinese holiday for the Hong Kong handover next week, dealers said on Friday.

China National Nonferrous Metals Import and Export Corp (CNIEC) is shipping 10,000 tonnes of copper that is due to arrive in Singapore in early July and South Korea's LG Metals has a further 10,000 tonnes expected in the middle of the month.
Dealers said copper premiums could dip to around $3-$5 a tonne over London Metal Exchange cash prices from around $15-$20 now if the metal was offloaded into the market here.
"The (LG Metals) cargo was offered to me at between $3 to $5 a tonne, depending on volume, but I have no need for it now," a Singapore copper dealer said.
On Thursday, an LG Metals spokesman in Seoul said the company had sold 10,000 tonnes of copper to European firm Metallgesellschaft and the cargo would be shipped to Singapore.
Another dealer confirmed earlier market talk of a Chinese copper shipment.
"CNIEC has arranged to send a 10,000-tonne copper shipment to Singapore," he said.
He warned, however, the shipment may be a game the Chinese firm is playing with the market and it may never discharge the cargo in Singapore.
"They may ship the same shipment back to China after just passing Singapore," he said.
If the Chinese shipment is really discharged the local copper premium could drop to as low as $5 a tonne, he added.
After closing on Friday night, Hong Kong and Chinese businesses will be on holiday until Thursday in observation of the Hong Kong handover to China.

"There won't be much trading by Chinese players in the early half of the next week," a Japanese dealer said. "It will be a different market and there can be many surprises, so people here are reluctant to trade."
Singapore premiums for western aluminium 20-25 kg ingots were quoted at $85-$90 a tonne over LME cash prices on Friday compared with last week's $90 a tonne.
Zinc premiums were in a range between $10 to $30, but both buyers and sellers are holding back from dealings, mainly due to the a lack of clear market direction.
"Neither (zinc) buyers nor sellers are willing to give-in and make deals," one trader said. "Looks like not just Chinese traders are in a holiday mood."
